transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I guess I came in because... for a long time now, I’ve been getting through my driving routes and my volunteer shifts alright, but there’s just this heavy, low feeling sitting on me most days. It's like I’m just going through the motions, you know, instead of really being in my own life.
How long have you been experiencing this heavy, low feeling?
It's been going on for about three years now. It started right around the time my father died, actually. I just haven't really shaken it since then.
Do you find yourself enjoying things you used to like before your father passed away?

I don't know if I've really noticed a difference there, to be honest. I guess I still like the same things okay. It's not really that I don't enjoy stuff anymore... I just always have that low mood kind of hanging around in the background.
Do you feel like you're able to take pleasure in the things you're doing, even if it's just okay?

Yeah, I guess so. I mean, I still get a kick out of a good cup of coffee on the road, or, you know, seeing the dogs when I volunteer at the shelter. The pleasure's still there, it's just... muted, maybe? Like I can enjoy those moments, but that heavy feeling is always waiting for me right after.
Have you noticed any change in your interest in activities or hobbies since your father passed away?

No, not really. I think I've pretty much kept up with everything I usually do. I haven't dropped any hobbies or stopped wanting to do things... I still do all my regular stuff when I'm off the road. It's just, like I said, I'm doing all of it with that low feeling kind of riding shotgun with me.
Have you noticed any change in your weight since your father passed away?
No, not really. My weight has stayed pretty much the same. I haven't noticed my clothes fitting any differently or anything like that, so I'd say it's been pretty steady.
Have you ever thought about ending your life since your father passed away?
No, no... nothing like that. I know I've been feeling down, but I've never had any thoughts about ending my life or hurting myself. It hasn't ever gotten to that point.
Have you noticed any change in how active or sluggish you've been since your father passed away?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I mean, I'm still doing my job, driving my routes, and keeping up with things at home. I don't feel like I'm moving in slow motion or, you know, overly restless or anything. I just feel down. But physically, my energy and how I'm moving around feels about the same as always.
Have you had any periods of at least two months where you didn't feel this low mood?
No, I don't think so. It's just... it's just been a constant thing. I haven't really had a break from feeling this way since he passed. It's just always there, you know?
Have you experienced any significant impairment in your social, occupational, or other areas of functioning due to this low mood?

Well, I'm still showing up for work and helping out at the pantry, so I'm getting things done. But... it just takes a lot more pushing than it used to. I really have to force myself to get going. 

And, well, I actually have an application for a logistics supervisor position that I started a while back, but I've just left it sitting unfinished. I just don't trust myself to keep up with the extra responsibility feeling like this. So, it hasn't stopped me from doing my day-to-day job, but it's definitely holding me back.
Have you noticed any difficulty in concentrating or making decisions since you've been feeling this low mood?

Yeah, I suppose I have. I mean, I can still do my job, but... lately I catch myself rereading delivery times, or I'll just be staring at the schedule board a lot longer than I should. It's just like my mind doesn't lock onto things the way it used to. I still get everything done, but I definitely have to double-check myself more to make sure I've got it right.
Do you often feel guilty or blame yourself for things?

No, not really. I don't think I struggle with guilt or blaming myself for things. I mean, I know I'm feeling down and not pushing myself like I used to, but I don't sit around feeling like it's my fault. So, no, I wouldn't say I deal with that.
Do you often feel worthless?

I don't know if worthless is the right word, but I do get pretty down on myself. I keep comparing myself to the kind of man my dad was. And... well, even though nobody is actually telling me I'm failing at things, I just hear it in my own head. I just feel like I should be further along by this age. Like I should be handling things better than this.
Have you ever had thoughts that you would be better off dead?

No. No, I've never had thoughts like that. I mean, I get pretty low, like I was just saying, but I don't want to die or anything. I've never felt like I'd be better off dead. It's just... I'm just tired of feeling stuck, I guess, but I definitely don't have those kinds of thoughts.
Have you ever felt like you're moving slower than you should be, or like you can't seem to calm down and are restless?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. I mean, I drive for a living, so I'm sitting behind the wheel a lot anyway, but... no, I don't feel like my body is moving slow or anything. And I'm not restless or pacing around, either. Physically, I feel pretty normal as far as all that goes.
Do you often find yourself expecting the worst in situations?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I'm not a particularly cheerful guy or anything, but I wouldn't say I'm always expecting the worst to happen. I just kind of take things as they come, you know? I don't really sit around worrying that everything is going to fall apart.
Have you had any days in the past year where you felt completely normal and didn't experience any of this low mood?

No, I don't think so. I mean... I can't really remember a day where I woke up and just felt completely normal, I guess. It's pretty much always there in the background. Like I was saying, it's not like I'm falling apart, but that low feeling doesn't really ever go away. I haven't really had a break from it.
Have you felt like you're a burden to others?

No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I go to work, I pay my bills, I take care of my own stuff... so I'm not really relying on anybody else to get by. It's just my own mood I'm dealing with. I don't feel like I'm dragging anyone else down or making them take care of me.
